title: Masked immigration officers arrest two passengers on crowded Sea-Tac jet bridge, delaying Alaska Airlines flight
excerpt: Masked immigration officers detained two passengers on a crowded jet bridge at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday, dragging at least one person away as travelers watched and delaying an Alaska Airlines flight to Los Angeles by nearly three hours.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Masked immigration officers detained two passengers on a crowded jet bridge at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday morning, dragging at least one person away as travelers watched and delaying an Alaska Airlines flight to Los Angeles by nearly three hours.

The confrontation unfolded around 8 a.m. Saturday at Gate N9 as passengers boarded Alaska Airlines Flight 1306, which had been scheduled to depart at 8:10 a.m. Video of the scene showed officers in unmarked jackets and khaki pants struggling with a person on the ground as passengers pressed against the jet bridge walls with their rolling suitcases.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said in a statement that its officers were conducting a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an immigrant from Mexico who the agency said overstayed his visa. During the confrontation, ICE said, another passenger, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, hurled hot coffee on the officers. The agency said she was also in the United States illegally from Mexico and had overstayed her visa, and that she could be charged with assaulting a federal officer.

A woman could be heard screaming on the video that her daughter was being taken and that the family has a work permit. A young girl was seen screaming on the jet bridge as her father was led away, according to witnesses. Officials have not confirmed whether a child was detained.

The Port of Seattle, which manages the airport, said it was outraged by the incident and that immigration enforcement actions at the airport are conducted without the Port's participation or knowledge. Alaska Airlines said it received no advance notice of the enforcement action and called the scene distressing for passengers and employees. The airline said it has raised concerns directly with the appropriate authorities and is working with the Port to see whether protocols were followed.

The flight's pilot left the aircraft and two flight attendants asked to be replaced, and the remaining passengers were deplaned before the flight eventually departed nearly three hours late.

The arrests are allegations, and those detained are presumed innocent until proven guilty in court.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar); Associated Press; CNN.
